# A chip list paints a square list-item surface behind each chip

Sub of #21329. Owned by @neo-opus-ada for the Engine 14 cut (Mon 23 Nov), so no curated labels: the chip tiles in neomjs/pages#109 wait on it.

## Context

Found while capturing the chip field's tile after PR #21352 merged. On `neo-theme-dark`, each chip in `examples/form/field/chip` sits on a square slate box whose corners show around the pill's rounded border. The `list-chip` tile already in neomjs/pages#109 shows the same boxes behind all six chips. The standalone `component-chip` tile has none: it is an outlined pill on the stage.

Measured on `dev` `557d2480d6` in devmode through the workbench's theme switch, on the chip field's first chip:

| Theme | List item background | Field background | Item radius | Chip radius, fill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `neo-theme-dark` | `rgb(51, 52, 61)` | `rgb(43, 43, 43)` | 0 | 15 px, transparent |
| `neo-theme-light` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` | 0 | 15 px, transparent |
| `neo-theme-neo-light` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` | 0 | 15 px, transparent |

The light themes hide the surface because it is white on a white field. Any theme whose item surface differs from the field shows it.

## Operator ruling (2026-11-18, on PR #21369)

The first fix, a transparent rest surface (PR #21369 at `889f26674b`), passed review and was then rejected by @tobiu:

- Chips need a fill for contrast, above all inside a chip field. The dark fill was right; its square corners were the defect. The exact color stays open to challenge.
- Text in a chip without a glyph touches the pill's left border.
- The chip list's `1px solid #ddd` frame reads near-white on a dark theme.

## The Problem

`list.Chip` renders each chip, a `component.Chip` with a 15 px radius, a 1 px border and no fill, inside a list item. The list paints that item with the theme's item surface, which is square, and its hover and active surfaces are square too. A chip has no fill of its own, so on a light theme (white item surface) it is an outline only. Its text has no spacing of its own: the glyph and the close button carry 7.5 px margins, so a glyph-less chip's text starts at the border. The chip list frames itself with a hard-coded `1px solid #ddd`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/css/src/list/Base.css`: `.neo-list .neo-list-item` takes `background-color: var(--list-item-background-color)`, with `-hover`, `-active` and `-selected` variants.
- The neo themes declare those variables on `:where(.neo-theme-*)` (zero specificity), the classic themes on `:root .neo-theme-*` (0,2,0). A workbench's example component carries its own theme class, so a classic theme's declaration out-ranks one set on `.neo-chip-list` itself. The item carries no theme class.
- `resources/css/src/list/Chip.css` already paints a selected chip's fill on the chip (`background-color: inherit !important` on the item).
- The item and its chip share one box (`.neo-chip-list .neo-list-item` has no padding). `--chip-border-radius` is `15px` in all four themes.
- `component.Chip` renders glyph, text and close button, and drops the glyph (`removeDom`) without an `iconCls`.
- The chip field's value list is a `list.Chip` with `border: 0` (`resources/css/src/form/field/Chip.css`), so a frame change leaves the field alone.
- Every other list frames itself through `--list-container-border`: `0` on `theme-light`, `none` on both neo themes, `1px solid #282829` on `theme-dark`.

## The Fix

- Each theme's `component/Chip.css` gains `--chip-background-color`: `#33343d` on `theme-dark` and `var(--sem-color-bg-neutral-highlighted)` on `theme-neo-dark` (the dark item surfaces the operator kept), `#eef0f3` on `theme-light`, `var(--gray-100)` on `theme-neo-light`. `.neo-chip` fills itself with it.
- In a chip list, the item declares `--list-item-background-color: var(--chip-background-color)` and takes `border-radius: var(--chip-border-radius)`, and the chip stays clear: the fill sits inside the pill, and the list's hover, active and selected surfaces still reach it.
- `.neo-chip-text:first-child` and `:last-child` keep the glyph's and the close button's 7.5 px from the border.
- `.neo-chip-list` takes `border: var(--list-container-border)` instead of `1px solid #ddd`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: In all four themes, a chip list's chip at rest shows `--chip-background-color` inside the pill: the item's background equals the token, its radius equals the chip's, and the chip itself is clear.
- [ ] AC-2: Hover changes the pill's surface, and a selected chip keeps its selected fill.
- [ ] AC-3: A chip without a glyph keeps at least 7 px between its border and its text.
- [ ] AC-4: The chip list's frame is the theme's `--list-container-border`, never the `#ddd` literal.
- [ ] AC-5: A browser spec covers AC-1 to AC-4 in all four themes, with the list carrying its own theme class: red on base, green at head.
- [ ] AC-6: Post-merge: the `form-field-chip` and `list-chip` tiles are recaptured on the fix and land in neomjs/pages#109.

## Out of Scope

- The chip field wrapping its triggers onto a row of their own once its chips fill the first row: #21381. On `dev` the 300 px example's first row is already full (its input sits at its 80 px minimum), so the text inset pushes it over.
- `theme-cyberpunk`: it ships no chip sheet.

## Avoided Traps

- A transparent rest surface, the first fix: rejected, a chip needs a fill for contrast.
- Declaring the item token on `.neo-chip-list`: a classic theme class on the list element out-ranks it.
- Leaving the chip's own fill on inside the list: it would cover the item's hover and active surfaces.
- `!important` overrides: none added.
